name: Lasagne
summary: Layers of pasta, slow-simmered beef and tomato sauce and creamy white sauce, baked under golden cheese.
about: Lasagne came to South African family tables from Italian cooking. Made ahead and cut into squares, it is a birthday-dinner and bring-a-dish favourite.

ingredients.name: Dried lasagne sheets
ingredients.note: the kind that needs no pre-cooking

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the onions and carrots, stirring, until soft, 8–10 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Turn the heat to high, add the mince and break it up with a wooden spoon. Cook until browned and the liquid has cooked away, 8–10 minutes.

Add the herbs, tomatoes, tomato paste, stock, sugar, salt and pepper. Simmer, partly covered, on low for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick. Keep it a little saucier than for spaghetti, because the pasta drinks up liquid.

For the white sauce, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute until bubbling. Take it off the heat and whisk in the milk a little at a time. Return to medium heat and whisk for 5–6 minutes, until it boils and thickly coats a spoon. Season with the nutmeg and salt and stir in a third of the cheese.

Heat the oven to 180 °C (160 °C if your oven is a fan oven). Spread a thin layer of meat sauce in a deep 30 × 20 cm dish. Cover with lasagne sheets, broken to fit and not overlapping, then a third of the remaining meat and a quarter of the white sauce. Repeat twice more, then finish with a layer of sheets, the last of the white sauce and the remaining cheese.
Bake for 40–45 minutes, until the top is golden and bubbling and a knife slides easily through the pasta. Cover loosely with foil if the top browns too fast.
Let it stand for 10–15 minutes so the layers hold when you cut it. Serve with a green salad.
prepNote: Assemble up to a day ahead and refrigerate; add 15 minutes to the baking time.
